title: SCP region Deny with INVERTED operator polarity (positive StringEquals footgun)
note: S4-guardrail-polarity: a region-guardrail SCP Deny whose aws:RequestedRegion condition uses a POSITIVE comparator (StringEquals) instead of the intended negated StringNotEquals. In a Deny a positive comparator fires WHEN the requested Region matches, so this policy denies actions ONLY inside {ap-south-1} and PERMITS every other region - the INVERSE of a region lock, the exact StringEquals/StringNotEquals footgun. Byte-for-byte this looked identical to a correct StringNotEquals lock before the fix and was credited as protective (appears:narrows). The evaluator must inspect operator polarity, narrate the inverted effect ('permits every region except...'), record the listed set as DENIED (never as allowedRegions), and flag it as a misconfiguration hazard (severity medium, hazard=true, regionPositiveOperator=true), just as rcp.js raises the inverted-org-scope hazard. The ceiling-not-grant invariant still holds: zero capability edges, no escalation, states SCPs set ceilings and do not grant.
